author: mindmap-write
readerQuestion: How much can I borrow in 2027 before it's a jumbo loan? [verb-only - no PAA, no completions]

presentation.reason: Finite down-payment cases show the jumbo line; a table of purchase prices by down payment answers it without inputs, and the existing down-payment calculator covers custom inputs.

interaction.reason: A fixed finite set of cases; a static table answers faster than inputs

animation.reason: Static scannable layout answers faster; no sequence to animate

decisionGap: Readers cannot see what home price the 2027 limit actually supports at their down payment, or whether waiting for January helps.
finding: FHFA (2026-11-24): 2027 baseline one-unit limit $855,400 (up $22,650 from $832,750), ceiling $1,283,100 in high-cost areas, $1,283,100 baseline and $1,924,650 ceiling in Alaska, Hawaii, Guam and the USVI; higher in all but 24 counties. In our internal calculation (limit / (1 - down payment share)) a loan at the $855,400 limit finances a price up to $881,856 / $900,421 / $950,444 / $1,006,353 / $1,069,250 at 3/5/10/15/20 percent down.
conditions: Baseline-county table is a floor for counties above baseline; one-unit properties only; ignores financed fees such as FHA-type premiums, closing costs and lender-set jumbo thresholds; FHFA says the limits apply to mortgages Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac can acquire in 2027; the lender decides which year's limit a loan falls under. CORRECTION (audit R1): FHFA says 2027 limits are higher than 2026 limits in all but 24 counties or county equivalents; it does NOT state how many counties exceed the $855,400 baseline. The earlier reading of that sentence as "limit above baseline in all but 24 counties" was wrong and is removed. Page says most counties use $855,400 and high-cost counties run up to $1,283,100.
whatWouldChange: A county limit above $855,400, a lender that sets its own threshold, or a documented Enterprise delivery-date rule (none verified).
caseDecisions: Retrieved cases.json for this question: no approved client record on this site matches (site _experience.md lists no named-client specifics). No client claim used; none forced.
whyNoQuantitativeAnalysis: Not applicable: this packet is basis calculated; the table is computed by calc.py (see execution.output). The FHFA limits themselves are reported facts.
reasoning: FHFA release is the source of every limit. The table is calculated from them.
method: price = limit / (1 - down payment share), run by calc.py on the FHFA limits
units: US dollars (purchase price) and share of price
limitations: Ignores financed fees, closing costs, mortgage insurance premiums that are financed, multi-unit limits, county limits other than the two modeled cases, and lender overlays.
counterexample: In a county whose limit is above $855,400, the same formula with that limit gives a higher price; a financed FHA-type premium lowers the price a conforming loan supports.

provenance.scopeAndLimits: baseline and high-cost ceiling cases; ignores financed fees
provenance.publicMethod: Formula and inputs stated beside the table
provenance.placement: Purchase Price Before a Loan Becomes Jumbo

sourceLimits: FHFA release read by fetch with verbatim quotes in this run; no delivery-date rule verified; AUDIT re-reads the FHFA page. Audit R1: county-count misreading corrected.
